Tripod derives from Greek tripous, tripodos “three-footed”, containing the three element tri; it can designate a three-legged support.
Trireme is from Latin triremis, tri- “three” plus remus “oar”; it denotes an ancient ship with three ranks of oars.
Trisect is tri- “three” plus Latin sectus “cut”; it means divide into three, especially equal, parts.

Triskaidekaphobia derives from Greek treiskaideka/triskaideka “thirteen”, treis “three” plus kai “and” plus deka “ten”. Tri is the historical three stem within the borrowed numeral, not an independently prefixed three in the English word.
Trisomic is the adjective of trisomy, itself from trisome (tri- plus the chromosome ending); the extra chromosome produces three copies of a particular chromosome.
Tristich denotes three lines of verse; tri- “three” plus stich “line”, ultimately Greek stichos.
Trisyllable is tri- “three” plus syllable, a word with three syllables.
Tritheism is tri- plus theism, belief in three gods. The tri- component means three, without asserting this is equivalent to every trinitarian doctrine.
Tritone in music is from Greek tri- “three” plus tonos “tone”: an interval of three whole tones, rather than three simultaneous notes.
Triune is tri- plus Latin unus “one”, meaning three in one.
Trivalent means having valence three or other domain-specific threefold values; it is tri- plus valent.
